person_note: The Goodreads evidence repeatedly exposes Harriet as a participating I-narrator in both present scenes and retrospective material. Dialogue and universal-you aphorisms are local material, not second-person narration; q08017’s internal “you” is likewise embedded thought. Authorized excerpts independently show first-person narration in the opening and Chapter 6, while whole-book study-guide evidence says Harriet narrates the novel across its differently titled past and present chapters. The structural alternation is temporal, not an alternation of narrative person, and no credible contrary person evidence was found.
